name: Graham Neubig
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: Post-training and scaffolding are more likely where the lever is; academia lacks compute for the pre-training-scale track, which is not his bet
D01.late_modes: Relying purely on piling up parameters is already too late; it is locked up by the few labs that own base models

D02.one_line: Not a direction he works on himself, but it fits his framework of post-training taking over from pre-training, and he would first ask how rigorous the evaluation design behind RL's score gains is
D02.late_modes: Work that merely finds a prompting trick that raises scores is already too late and is soon absorbed by the next generation of models

D03.one_line: His own Agent Workflow Memory shows that training-free, model-agnostic mechanisms are a contribution academia can truly own independently
D03.late_modes: RSI that needs large-scale online self-improvement is kept out of academia by the compute threshold; lightweight training-free mechanisms are not yet too late
D03.conflict: His own paper and his company's business model both rest on the judgment that lightweight mechanisms work

D04.one_line: This is his home turf, but he concedes that complex scaffolding is being absorbed by vendor CLIs and model capability, and only the evaluation and orchestration-management layer holds up
D04.late_modes: Tuning prompts and designing orchestration logic is already too late; the front row is almost entirely vendor CLIs
D04.conflict: His company All Hands AI is itself a commercial venture in this direction

D05.one_line: This is the one craft in his career that has not depreciated: credibility needs rigor, not a compute advantage, and academia has a structural incentive to do this debunking work
D05.late_modes: A new benchmark built only to land a top-conference paper and abandoned after publication is already too late: one that is not kept in use might as well never have happened
D05.conflict: OpenHands's reputation is built on evaluation being credible

D06.one_line: No judgment: it is not something he studies; the methodology of evaluation credibility could in principle transfer, but he has never publicly discussed embodied content

D07.one_line: No judgment: diffusion/flow policy and world action models are outside what he has publicly discussed

D08.one_line: No judgment: vision and language was one of his early research directions, but there has been no public output in recent years, so no judgment on architectures such as JEPA

D09.one_line: No judgment on the content, but honestly diagnosing the gap between simulation and reality has the same structure as his SWE-Bench contamination critique, and he would suggest entering from that angle

D10.one_line: No judgment: no public material shows him ever discussing autonomous driving, and there is no methodological connection point to extend from

D11.one_line: No judgment: vision and language and semantic grounding were directions he listed, but there is no evidence of continuation in recent years

D12.one_line: No judgment: no record of him discussing diffusion or image/video generation was found in the public material

D13.one_line: No judgment: no public material shows him discussing interpretability, alignment or safety

D14.one_line: Not a specific field he has publicly discussed, but academic low-level tools of the FlashAttention kind being adopted as standard industry equipment is exactly the path he has followed since DyNet

D15.one_line: No judgment: no public material shows him discussing AI for Science, and there is no methodological connection point

D16.one_line: No judgment: no public material shows him discussing recommender systems or retrieval, which is outside his research scope

lever_reason: Evaluation credibility decides whether the other levers are really working; scaffolding does not count as an independent lever and will be flattened quickly by model capability, so it is not given a separate weight

Q2.condition: Narrow domain, not general LLM pre-training; credible third-party evaluation exists in that domain; compute reaches months of continuous scale; open weights with a path to outside adoption; all four must hold to count as high impact

cruxes.question: Is evaluation and credibility really the lever most worth betting on, or a consolation prize for those with few resources?
cruxes.my_position: Evaluation credibility decides whether you can tell if the other levers are really working; it is a precondition, not a consolation prize
cruxes.would_change_if: A direction built purely on compute and data scale, without carefully designed evaluation, crushes a carefully evaluated direction for two years in a row

cruxes.question: Is the cleverness of complex multi-agent orchestration really being quickly flattened by model capability?
cruxes.my_position: The design advantage of complex orchestration has a shelf life measured in months; model capability will flatten this kind of advantage within a generation or two
cruxes.would_change_if: An independent open-source harness beats the vendor's own CLI on raw scores consistently for over a year, and is not a flash in the pan

cruxes.question: Is training foundation models in a school lab with GPUs the highest-impact path for students from undergraduate to master's level?
cruxes.my_position: Yes when the domain is narrow, weights are open, credible third-party evaluation exists and compute is at scale, but this is not an unconditional claim that academia can also win the pre-training war
cruxes.would_change_if: An academic team trains a widely adopted foundation model without meeting these conditions, showing the conditions were set too strictly

taste_advice: Define yourself as someone who can design honest evaluations that cannot be won by leaderboard-chasing, not as someone who does agents or embodied AI

pairwise.why: Evaluation credibility is a precondition; without it you cannot even say whether D08's progress is real
By the same logic: credible measurement is his moat, and he does not bet on embodied content itself
The final test of embodied AI is whether tasks succeed on real robots, which is easier to falsify than the potential of representation learning
A policy that produces actions directly can be checked right or wrong on control tasks, which is easier to test than pure representation prediction
Honestly diagnosing the gap between simulation and reality is at least a problem one can enter from the angle of evaluation credibility
His own Agent Workflow Memory shows that academia can make independent contributions with this kind of mechanism
Vision and language was a direction he listed; generation has no connection at all
Evaluation is the academic stronghold he recognizes; academia lacks compute on the pre-training-scale track, and he never bets on that line
D04's complex scaffolding is being absorbed by vendor CLIs; lightweight mechanisms like D03 have a longer half-life, and he has verified this himself
Evaluation is the only field he has worked in deeply; alignment and interpretability are outside what he has publicly discussed
RoboNLP was one of the research directions he listed; autonomous driving never appears in his material
